mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate level compresses the discount rate for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower borrowing costs and increased liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods with FEDFUNDS in the lowest quartile of its historical range, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market that fuels wage growth and inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, strong housing starts (HOUST) and robust consumer spending (RSAFS) signal overheating, leading to a higher probability of Fed tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 1350 and RSAFS > 700000, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production (INDPRO) level indicates strengthening manufacturing activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods with INDPRO above its 50-period moving average, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 305 (index value), it signals persistent inflation that may lead to aggressive Fed tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 305, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high inflation rate (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) combined with a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 4.5%) indicates a delayed policy response, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate aggressive tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.5 and FEDFUNDS < 4.5, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In labor market recovery phases, a high employment level (PAYEMS > 156000) and a low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.0%) signal improving economic conditions that boost corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS > 156000 and UNRATE < 4.0, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
